metadata.hardware_requirements: computing server with NVIDIA Quadro K620 GPU and Intel Xeon CPU E5-1650 (3.6 GHz, 6 cores)

nodes_source.source_quote: The data used to support the results of this study are available from the corresponding author upon request.
nodes_source.description: Real-world traffic data, including traffic volumes and driving behaviors from the Qingdao and Huangdao freeway, used to calibrate the SUMO simulator.
nodes_source.reproducibility_rationale: Data availability statement explicitly specifies that the data is available upon request from the corresponding author, with no URL or repository provided.

nodes_process.source_quote: The simulation parameters regarding driving behaviors are calibrated based on empirical data.
nodes_process.description: SUMO traffic simulation environment is configured using real road networks, with vehicle behaviour parameters calibrated using empirical dataset. Speed limits set to 80 km/h (mainline) and 40 km/h.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, most tools named, major physical simulation bounds are provided though microscopic behavioral calibration is vague.

nodes_process.source_quote: Three consecutive frames of the traffic video in the controlled area are needed... After zooming and down-sampling, the size of one observation is 4x512 in pixels.
nodes_process.description: Vehicle locations from traffic frames are extracted, zoomed, and down-sampled to form a position matrix of 4x512. Three frames are stacked for temporal features.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, visual geometry params stated precisely but generic unstated tool is assumed.

nodes_process.source_quote: The Q-network is trained in 10^6 training frames... The gradient-based algorithm Adam is used to update wi to minimize the loss function.
nodes_process.description: DQN agent trained over 1e6 simulation frames to optimize ramp metering rate using multitask loss for speed and queues. Employs epsilon-greedy policy, Adam optimizer, target network, replay buffer.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, comprehensive params provided in table 1; algorithmic layout explicitly diagrammed.

nodes_process.source_quote: each scenario is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments. The simulations for the training phase and each experiment are initialized with different random seeds.
nodes_process.description: Compare metrics among DRL policy, no control, and PI-ALINEA algorithm using 20 simulated runs under variable random seeds.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=4, control logic baselines fully instantiated with specific parameters; sample sizing clear.

nodes_process.source_quote: missing information for each subarea is evaluated in 20 simulation experiments with perturbed data... information in the subarea is removed from original data
nodes_process.description: Simulation frames mask one of eight specific regional segments prior to inference. Examines impact of losing video metadata over twenty independent runs.
nodes_process.reproducibility_rationale: clarity=3, logic well formed but missing explicit numerical box bounds for spatial occlusions.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The training process, presented in Figure 8, can be finished in less than 24 hours on a computing server
nodes_sink.description: Convergence curves for (a) episode reward and (b) mean travel time over the 1,000,000 training frames.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Hyperparameters and network structure are detailed, but the raw traffic video dataset is 'available upon request' and exact implementation source code is omitted, limiting independent reproduction.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 9 presents the Q1 (25%), Q2 (50%), and Q3 (75%) of the travel times in the mainline for three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Vehicle travel times over the simulation period across the mainline for no control, PI-ALINEA, and Deep RL strategies.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clear comparison methodology inside SUMO, but underlying input traffic dataset is private and code is unreleased.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Table 2 presents mean vehicle travel times in 20 simulation experiments.
nodes_sink.description: Mean vehicle travel times (in seconds) and percentage difference vs No Controls in 20 randomized simulation experiments for No controls, PI-ALINEA, and DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Results directly derived from multiple random-seed SUMO experiments, but base configuration data lacks open access.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 10 presents the temporal-spatial distribution of the mean speeds along the mainline.
nodes_sink.description: Heat maps indicating mean speed at spatial offsets over the simulation period, comparing (a) no control, (b) PI-ALINEA, and (c) DRL.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Outputs match conventional traffic simulator aggregates, structurally coherent but hampered by closed simulation environments/datasets.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 11 presents the Q1, Q2, and Q3 of the queue lengths at the on-ramp in three scenarios.
nodes_sink.description: Distribution curves with quantile shading indicating varying on-ramp queue lengths over the 1-hour span.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Appropriately illustrates secondary congestion impacts using defined reward metrics, but bound by overall lack of code sharing.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 12 presents the mean queue lengths at the on-ramp and the red ratios (i.e., the proportion of the red phase in the simulation time)
nodes_sink.description: Scatter plot correlating simulation red signal ratios against formed on-ramp queue lengths for PI-ALINEA and Deep RL approaches.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Coherent comparison combining signal ratio limits vs queue results, relying on identical unreleased inputs as main tables.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 13 presents the queue lengths at the on-ramp and the occupancy downstream of the merging area for the two ramp metering methods.
nodes_sink.description: Timeseries overlays showing synchronicity between target main-lane occupancy and local on-ramp queue lengths.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Clearly represents downstream tracking limits in closed-loop systems; data unavailable directly.

nodes_sink.source_quote: The better performance of the proposed DRL method is further revealed when considering traffic flows downstream of the merge area, which is demonstrated in Figure 14.
nodes_sink.description: Box-and-whisker volume traces reporting measured hourly vehicles output at 5-minute sampling rates downstream.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: Extracted traffic volumes directly from validated SUMO output flows; code/data not fully provided.

nodes_sink.source_quote: Figure 16 presents the box plot of travel time when the information of different subareas is removed, and the baseline is the result of experiments that take original data as input.
nodes_sink.description: Sensitivity or perturbation results: box plots of overall mainline travel times under the condition that DRL input state ignores certain specific numbered subregions from the upstream inputs.
nodes_sink.reproducibility_rationale: The exact masking mechanism across position matrices is loosely outlined without code parameters, making this specific ablation slightly harder to reproduce precisely.
